#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurity

100 days. One evidence trail.

Days 1–83 are represented in chronological order. Day topics confirmed by the project artifacts are labeled separately from the early AWS topics confirmed by the user but still awaiting the original archive artifact required by the canonical ledger.

83 of 100 days · current published phase: CI/CD & Observability.

Journey phases

From cloud foundations to integrated capstones.

Days 1–23

AWS Networking Foundations

Account, identity, compute, VPC networking, scaling, observability and infrastructure as code.

Days 24–40

Infrastructure Automation

Ansible from first playbooks through variables, roles, failure handling, collections and a LAMP capstone.

Days 41–52

Linux Administration

Filesystem, permissions, identity, processes, services, logs, scheduling, packages and hardening.

Days 53–60

Networking Deep Dive

Transport, DNS, DHCP, HTTP/TLS, reverse proxies, load balancing and layered troubleshooting.

Days 61–70

Docker

Images, containers, storage, networking, Compose, Dockerfiles, security and a multi-container capstone.

Days 71–82

Kubernetes

Control plane, workload controllers, Services, configuration, storage, ingress, Helm and production deployment.

Days 83–90

CI/CD & Observability

Delivery pipelines followed by metrics, dashboards and centralized logging.

Days 91–97

Cloud Security & DevSecOps

Shared responsibility, identity, secrets, detection, incident response and infrastructure hardening.

Days 98–100

Capstone

Integrated infrastructure, delivery, monitoring and security evidence.

DAY 83Published journey entry

CI/CD Foundations

CI/CD & Observability

CI/CD turns source changes into a repeatable delivery path where validation, build, test and deployment decisions are explicit instead of depending on manual release memory.

DAY 82Published artifact recovered

Kubernetes Production Deployment

Kubernetes

The Kubernetes capstone connected scope, configuration, secrets, controllers, probes, networking, storage, ingress and Helm into one production-style deployment flow.

DAY 81Published artifact recovered

Helm

Kubernetes

Helm packages Kubernetes templates, defaults and metadata into configurable releases so environment differences do not require copy-paste manifests.

DAY 80Published artifact recovered

Kubernetes Ingress

Kubernetes

Ingress describes HTTP/HTTPS routing rules toward Services; an Ingress controller is the component that actually implements those rules.

DAY 79Published artifact recovered

Kubernetes Persistent Storage

Kubernetes

PersistentVolumes, PersistentVolumeClaims and StorageClasses separate application data from the lifecycle of individual Pods.

DAY 78Published artifact recovered

Kubernetes Secrets

Kubernetes

Kubernetes Secrets provide a dedicated object for sensitive configuration, but confidentiality still depends on access control, storage protection and application behavior.

DAY 77Published artifact recovered

Kubernetes ConfigMaps

Kubernetes

ConfigMaps separate non-sensitive application configuration from container images and can deliver values as environment variables or projected files.

DAY 76Published journey entry

Kubernetes Namespaces

Kubernetes

Namespaces scope namespaced Kubernetes objects so environments and teams can organize resources without making object names globally unique across the cluster.

DAY 75Published artifact recovered

Kubernetes Services

Kubernetes

A Service gives changing Pods a stable network endpoint and selects its backend endpoints through labels.

DAY 74Published artifact recovered

Kubernetes Deployments

Kubernetes

Deployments sit above ReplicaSets to manage stateless application rollouts declaratively, including replacement strategy and revision history.

DAY 73Published artifact recovered

Kubernetes ReplicaSets

Kubernetes

ReplicaSets continuously maintain a requested number of matching Pods and recreate missing replicas from a Pod template.

DAY 72Published artifact recovered

Kubernetes Pods

Kubernetes

A Pod is Kubernetes' smallest deployable compute object and groups one or more tightly coupled containers that share a network context and selected storage.

DAY 71Published artifact recovered

Kubernetes Architecture

Kubernetes

Kubernetes is a set of cooperating control-plane and node components that continuously reconcile declared state into running workloads.

DAY 70Published artifact recovered

Multi-Container Deployment

Docker

The Docker capstone connected image build, private networking, persistent storage, health checks, secrets and runtime hardening into one small application system.

DAY 69Published journey entry

Container Security

Docker

Container security reduces what a compromised application can do by removing unnecessary identity, filesystem, capability and host privileges.

DAY 68Published artifact recovered

Dockerfiles

Docker

A Dockerfile is an ordered build recipe that turns source and dependencies into an image layer by layer.

DAY 67Published artifact recovered

Docker Compose

Docker

Docker Compose describes a multi-container application, its network, storage, environment and startup relationships in one version-controlled file.

DAY 66Published artifact recovered

Docker Networks

Docker

User-defined Docker networks let containers discover one another by names or aliases instead of coupling applications to replaceable container IP addresses.

DAY 65Published journey entry

Docker Volumes

Docker

Volumes keep important state outside an individual container's writable layer so container replacement does not have to mean data loss.

DAY 64Published artifact recovered

Docker Container Lifecycle

Docker

A container combines an image with runtime configuration, a primary process and a writable layer whose lifecycle differs from both the image and durable storage.

DAY 63Published journey entry

Docker Images

Docker

Docker images are content-addressed, layered filesystem artifacts used as immutable bases for containers; tags are movable labels while digests identify exact image content.

DAY 62Published artifact recovered

Docker Architecture

Docker

Docker is a client-server system: the CLI sends API requests, the daemon manages Docker objects and registries distribute images.

DAY 61Published journey entry

Why Containers

Docker

Containers package an application with its userspace dependencies while isolating processes on a shared host kernel, reducing environment drift without pretending each workload is a virtual machine.

DAY 60Published artifact recovered

Network Troubleshooting Sequence

Networking Deep Dive

Troubleshooting becomes repeatable when a failed request is traced through DNS, routing, transport, TLS, proxy, backend and system pressure one layer at a time.

DAY 59Published artifact recovered

Load Balancing Concepts

Networking Deep Dive

Load balancing spreads requests across backends, but availability depends on health semantics, session state and every shared dependency that remains.

DAY 58Published artifact recovered

Nginx Reverse Proxy

Networking Deep Dive

A reverse proxy accepts client traffic and forwards it to application backends, moving routing, TLS and client-identity trust into an explicit infrastructure boundary.

DAY 57Published artifact recovered

TLS 1.3 Handshake

Networking Deep Dive

Before encrypted application traffic starts, TLS negotiates keys and lets the client validate the server certificate chain and requested hostname.

DAY 56Published artifact recovered

HTTP vs HTTPS

Networking Deep Dive

HTTPS is HTTP carried inside a TLS-protected connection, adding confidentiality, integrity and authenticated server identity to the transport path.

DAY 55Published artifact recovered

DHCP

Networking Deep Dive

DHCP automatically leases clients network configuration through the Discover, Offer, Request and Acknowledge exchange.

DAY 54Published artifact recovered

DNS & Cloud Security

Networking Deep Dive

DNS turns names into records through caches and recursive resolution, making name resolution both an availability dependency and a security boundary.

DAY 53Published artifact recovered

TCP vs UDP

Networking Deep Dive

TCP provides a reliable ordered byte stream; UDP provides independent best-effort datagrams with lower protocol overhead and different application responsibilities.

DAY 52Published artifact recovered

Linux Hardening

Linux Administration

Linux hardening reduces exposed services and privilege while keeping the effective security state observable and supportable.

DAY 51Published artifact recovered

Linux Networking Tools

Linux Administration

Linux networking tools become useful when used in an order that proves interfaces, routes, listeners and application reachability instead of as random commands.

DAY 50Published artifact recovered

Bash Scripting Automation

Linux Administration

Bash turns repeated Linux commands into automation only when inputs, quoting, exit behavior and failure visibility are designed deliberately.

DAY 49Published artifact recovered

SSH Deep Dive

Linux Administration

SSH combines remote access, key authentication and host verification, but small permission or trust mistakes can make secure access fail or become unsafe.

DAY 48Published journey entry

apt & dnf

Linux Administration

Package managers resolve repositories, dependencies and installed state, turning software lifecycle into something the operating system can track.

DAY 47Published journey entry

Cron vs systemd Timers

Linux Administration

Scheduled work needs more than a time expression: execution environment, missed-run behavior, logging and dependencies determine whether a scheduler is reliable.

DAY 46Published journey entry

journald

Linux Administration

journald turns service and kernel events into queryable operational evidence instead of leaving troubleshooting to memory and guesswork.

DAY 45Published journey entry

systemd

Linux Administration

systemd manages service lifecycle, dependencies and startup state so long-running processes are supervised rather than left to terminal sessions.

DAY 44Published journey entry

Processes & Signals

Linux Administration

Processes are running programs with identities, resources and parent-child relationships; signals are one of the operating system's ways to request or force state changes.

DAY 43Published journey entry

Users, Groups & sudo

Linux Administration

Linux identity management separates users, groups and delegated privilege so administrative access does not have to mean sharing root.

DAY 42Published journey entry

Linux Permissions

Linux Administration

Permissions and ownership determine which users and groups can read, modify or execute files and directories.

DAY 41Published journey entry

Linux Filesystem

Linux Administration

The Linux phase began with the filesystem layout: where configuration, logs, variable data, devices and user data live and why location communicates purpose.

DAY 40Published journey entry

LAMP Automation Capstone

Infrastructure Automation

The Ansible phase closed by combining roles for common setup, Apache, PHP and MySQL into a deployable LAMP stack with Vault, handlers and failure recovery.

DAY 39Published artifact recovered

Ansible Galaxy Collections

Infrastructure Automation

Collections package modules, plugins, roles, playbooks and documentation so teams can reuse maintained automation instead of rebuilding every integration from scratch.

DAY 38Published artifact recovered

Blocks, Rescue & Always

Infrastructure Automation

Blocks group related tasks, `rescue` provides controlled recovery for task failures inside the block, and `always` guarantees cleanup or logging paths.

DAY 37Published after ledger snapshot

Ansible Loops

Infrastructure Automation

Loops reduce repetitive tasks while keeping each item visible in Ansible's result model.

DAY 36Published after ledger snapshot

Ansible Handlers

Infrastructure Automation

Handlers trigger follow-up actions such as service reloads only when notifying tasks actually change something.

DAY 35Published after ledger snapshot

Jinja2 Templates

Infrastructure Automation

Jinja2 templates generate configuration from variables so the structure is reusable while environment-specific values remain data.

DAY 34Published journey entry

Conditionals in Ansible

Infrastructure Automation

Conditionals make tasks depend on facts and results, while `failed_when` lets automation define what failure actually means for a command.

DAY 33Published journey entry

host_vars, group_vars & register

Infrastructure Automation

Real projects need static per-host/group data and runtime results without mixing both into one giant variable file.

DAY 32Published journey entry

Ansible Roles

Infrastructure Automation

Roles break large playbooks into reusable units with conventional locations for tasks, handlers, defaults, templates and files.

DAY 31Published journey entry

Ansible Facts

Infrastructure Automation

Facts let automation discover the host it is operating on instead of hard-coding assumptions about every machine.

DAY 30Published journey entry

Ansible Modules

Infrastructure Automation

Modules are Ansible's state-aware building blocks and are generally safer than converting every operation into shell commands.

DAY 29Published journey entry

Ansible Ad-Hoc Commands

Infrastructure Automation

Ad-hoc commands provide fast remote execution for small tasks without turning every inspection or one-time action into a playbook.

DAY 28Published journey entry

Ansible Patterns

Infrastructure Automation

Patterns decide which inventory hosts a command or play targets, making selection logic part of the safety model.

DAY 27Published journey entry

Ansible Inventory

Infrastructure Automation

Inventory is the model of what Ansible manages: hosts, groups and the connection data that lets automation reach the correct systems.

DAY 26Published journey entry

Ansible Variables

Infrastructure Automation

Variables separate changing data from reusable automation, but precedence decides which value Ansible ultimately uses.

DAY 25Topic verified by artifact

First Ansible Playbook

Infrastructure Automation

The first playbook moved from one-off commands to a declarative file that maps hosts to tasks and desired state.

DAY 24Topic verified by artifact

Introduction to Ansible

Infrastructure Automation

Ansible introduced configuration management as a way to describe and repeat system changes over SSH instead of maintaining a collection of one-off login rituals.

DAY 23Topic verified by artifact

Terraform Introduction

AWS Networking Foundations

Terraform introduced a provider-neutral infrastructure-as-code workflow built around configuration, plans and state.

DAY 22Topic verified by artifact

AWS CDK

AWS Networking Foundations

The AWS CDK lets infrastructure be modeled with programming-language constructs and synthesized into CloudFormation.

DAY 21Topic verified by artifact

AWS CloudFormation

AWS Networking Foundations

CloudFormation turns AWS infrastructure into templates and stacks so desired resources can be reviewed, repeated and changed deliberately.

DAY 20Topic verified by artifact

AWS Systems Manager

AWS Networking Foundations

Systems Manager provides managed operational channels for instances and nodes so administration does not have to revolve around exposed SSH access.

DAY 19Topic verified by artifact

AWS Config

AWS Networking Foundations

AWS Config records resource configuration state and can evaluate whether resources match defined compliance rules.

DAY 18Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

CloudTrail

AWS Networking Foundations

AWS CloudTrail records account activity so operators can answer who or what called an AWS API, when it happened, from where and against which resources.

DAY 17Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

CloudWatch

AWS Networking Foundations

Amazon CloudWatch introduced metrics, logs, alarms and dashboards so AWS resource and application health could be operated from evidence rather than intuition.

DAY 16Topic verified by artifact

Auto Scaling

AWS Networking Foundations

Auto Scaling Groups maintain a desired fleet and can change capacity in response to health and demand instead of treating one server as permanent.

DAY 15Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

Elastic Load Balancer

AWS Networking Foundations

Elastic Load Balancing introduced a stable traffic-distribution layer in front of multiple targets so application instances can be replaced and scaled without clients tracking each server directly.

DAY 14Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

Review + Practical Lab

AWS Networking Foundations

Day 14 consolidated the first networking concepts into a practical lab so identity, addressing, routing and filtering were tested as one path rather than memorized separately.

DAY 13Topic verified by artifact

Transit Gateway

AWS Networking Foundations

Transit Gateway replaces a growing mesh of point-to-point connections with a hub that can centralize routing between networks.

DAY 12Topic verified by artifact

VPC Peering

AWS Networking Foundations

VPC Peering connects two VPCs directly, but routing, addressing and security rules still decide whether applications can communicate.

DAY 11Topic verified by artifact

VPC Endpoints

AWS Networking Foundations

VPC Endpoints let workloads reach supported AWS services without making the public internet the required data path.

DAY 10Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

NAT Gateway

AWS Networking Foundations

A NAT Gateway lets private IPv4 workloads initiate outbound connections without making those workloads directly reachable from unsolicited internet traffic.

DAY 09Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

Internet Gateway

AWS Networking Foundations

An Internet Gateway gives a VPC a route target for direct internet connectivity, but instances still need the right addressing, routes and security policy.

DAY 08Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

Route Tables

AWS Networking Foundations

Route tables decide where packets leaving a subnet are sent by matching destination prefixes to targets such as local VPC routing, gateways or network connections.

DAY 07Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

Subnets

AWS Networking Foundations

Subnets divide a VPC address range into Availability-Zone-scoped network segments where routing and placement policy become concrete.

DAY 06Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

Amazon VPC

AWS Networking Foundations

Amazon VPC is the private network boundary where AWS workloads receive IP space, subnets, routing and network security controls.

DAY 05Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

Network ACLs

AWS Networking Foundations

Network ACLs add stateless allow/deny filtering at the subnet boundary, complementing rather than replacing stateful Security Groups.

DAY 04Topic verified by artifact

Security Groups

AWS Networking Foundations

Security Groups control allowed network flows around AWS network interfaces and workloads using stateful rules.

DAY 03Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

EC2

AWS Networking Foundations

EC2 introduced on-demand virtual servers and the practical connection between compute, images, instance types, storage, networking and secure remote administration.

DAY 02Topic verified by artifact

IAM & Least Privilege

AWS Networking Foundations

Identity comes before infrastructure: decide who can act, what they can do, and how narrowly that permission can be scoped.

DAY 01Topic confirmed · archive artifact pending

AWS Free Tier & AWS Console

AWS Networking Foundations

The journey began by learning the AWS account, billing and console boundaries before creating infrastructure that could quietly become a bill.
